name: Rules vs. outcomes
lowSummary: you hold to lines you won't cross, even when crossing them would lead to a better result.
highSummary: you judge actions mostly by their results, and you'll cross a line if it clearly reduces harm.

name: Everyone vs. my people
lowSummary: you try to count everyone equally, even when that costs the people closest to you.
highSummary: you protect the people closest to you, even at a real cost to others.

name: Principle vs. loyalty
lowSummary: honesty and justice come before covering for people you love.
highSummary: you stand by your people, even when the right thing to do is less clear.

name: Security vs. liberty
lowSummary: you're willing to trade personal freedom and privacy for safety.
highSummary: you'd rather keep freedom and privacy and accept more risk.

name: Need vs. merit
lowSummary: you think fairness means helping those with the greatest need, or treating everyone the same.
highSummary: you think fairness means people get what they've earned or deserve.

name: Self vs. others
lowSummary: you guard your own life and wellbeing, and you think that's legitimate.
highSummary: you're prepared to give up a great deal of your own life for others.

name: Experience vs. reality
lowSummary: how life feels matters more to you than whether it's real.
highSummary: a real life with real struggle matters more to you than a perfect illusion.

name: Narrow vs. wide moral circle
lowSummary: moral concern belongs mainly to humans.
highSummary: moral concern extends well beyond humans, to animals and possibly machines.

name: How you learn
lowSummary: you learn best from instruction, demonstration, or theory before you start.
highSummary: you learn best by diving in and figuring it out.
lowShift: you want more instruction up front

name: How you teach
lowSummary: you teach by explaining clearly and showing the way.
highSummary: you teach by asking questions and letting people find the answer.
highShift: you lean more on questions and discovery

name: How you lead
lowSummary: you bring people into decisions rather than making them alone.
highSummary: you step up, decide, and tell people what to do.

name: How you handle conflict
lowSummary: you keep the peace and let small things go.
highSummary: you raise problems directly, even when it's uncomfortable.
lowShift: you hold back and keep the peace

name: How you decide
lowSummary: you trust your judgment and move quickly.
highSummary: you look for facts before you commit.

name: How you take criticism
lowSummary: you stand behind your work when it's criticized.
highSummary: you treat criticism as information and separate it from yourself.

name: How much you take on
lowSummary: you protect your time and keep to your own responsibilities.
highSummary: you take on whatever needs doing, even when it isn't yours.
lowShift: you hold your boundaries more firmly
highShift: you take on more than your share

name: Supporting people
lowSummary: you hold people to clear expectations and consequences.
highSummary: you coach people and look for why they're struggling.
highShift: you lean toward coaching and support

name: How you solve problems
lowSummary: you analyze and plan before you act.
highSummary: you experiment, try things, and adjust as you go.

name: How you delegate
lowSummary: you give important work to people who've already proven themselves.
highSummary: you give people work that stretches them.
lowShift: you give important work to proven people
highShift: you give people more room to stretch
